refutations.argument: The stipulation (and the rule's applies_when) triggers whenever more than one player lost the previous game, without excluding drawn games. Official sources settle a three-player game in which one player concedes (104.3a: that player loses) and the two remaining players then lose simultaneously: 104.4a makes that game a draw. More than one player 'lost', so the stipulation says the first loser (the conceder) chooses; but 103.1 says that after a draw the player who made the choice in that game chooses. The case's own rule text leaves both answers applying to the same game, so it gives a result the official draw sentence contradicts, and step 4 ('leaves this as it is') cannot be true for this draw. The draw sentence is the specific, official provision and prevails over a stipulation; the proposed rule never says the draw clause takes priority, so as worded it overbroadly captures drawn multiplayer games.

source.excerpt: A player who concedes leaves the game immediately. That player loses the game.

steps.conclusion: In a three-player game where one player concedes, that player lost the game, so C3's condition 'more than one player lost' can be met by a game that later ends in a draw.

source.excerpt: If all the players remaining in a game lose simultaneously, the game is a draw.

steps.conclusion: If the two remaining players lose simultaneously, the game is a draw although a player lost earlier.

source.excerpt: If the previous game was a draw, the player who made the choice in that game makes the choice in this game.

steps.conclusion: For that drawn game 103.1 gives the choice to the player who chose in it, while C3 gives it to the first loser (the conceder): the proposed rule conflicts with 103.1 on a game the official sources settle.
